findings:
🟠 [r2-cgroup-setm-stdin-inherit] MUST-FIX Enabling `set -m` before the `systemd-run --scope ... &` launch in run_worker's cgroup branch changes worker stdin semantics: without job control bash redirects async commands' stdin from /dev/null, with job control on the worker now inherits the dispatcher's stdin (tty or harness pipe). Impact on the primary production path: a worker that reads stdin can consume the dispatcher's input or, when stdin is a tty, take SIGTTIN and sit stopped until the wall timeout fires; the previous cgroup behavior was always /dev/null. Smallest remediation: add an explicit `</dev/null` to the systemd-run launch line (and mirror via the sync script) so the pgid isolation is gained without the stdin change.
🔵 [r2-detached-test-never-hits-cgroup] CUT/FOLLOW-UP assert_r2_cgroup_kill_failure_detached_real_path cannot exercise the new fallback: run_worker's IN_DETACHED_CHILD branch returns before the HAVE_CGROUP branch, so SCOPE_UNIT stays empty and the WORKER_SID path kills the worker regardless of HETERO_TEST_SYSTEMCTL_KILL_FAIL. The assertion is true but vacuous for R2; excluded because the spec asked for this case as written and detached runs genuinely never use cgroup containment, so no product failure exists.
🔵 [r6-positive-test-passes-via-pkill] CUT/FOLLOW-UP assert_r6_cancel_kills_when_cmdline_has_tag would also pass if _watchdog_sleeppid_cmdline_has_tag always returned false, because the retained tag-scoped pkill at the end of _cancel_worker_watchdog kills the tagged helper anyway; only the negative case discriminates the new check. Excluded as a test-strength item, not a product defect; a stronger version would assert the kill happened before the pkill line or call the helper function directly.
